sample_size.excerpt: A total of 48,137 men from the Health Professionals Follow-up Study were followed from 1986 to 2017.

cases.location: Table 2, Advanced prostate cancer, Model 2 case counts

effect_size.excerpt: Compared to never-users, men who took multivitamins ≥10 tablets per week were not at increased risk for advanced (HR [95% CI], 1.14 [0.77–1.70], P trend = 0.46), lethal (1.07 [0.80–1.44], P trend = 0.59), or high-grade (1.20 [0.88–1.63], P trend = 0.83) prostate cancer ( Table 2 ).
effect_size.location: Results, paragraph 2; Table 2, Advanced prostate cancer, Model 2

confidence_interval.excerpt: Compared to never-users, men who took multivitamins ≥10 tablets per week were not at increased risk for advanced (HR [95% CI], 1.14 [0.77–1.70], P trend = 0.46), lethal (1.07 [0.80–1.44], P trend = 0.59), or high-grade (1.20 [0.88–1.63], P trend = 0.83) prostate cancer ( Table 2 ).

p_value.excerpt: In terms of duration, multivitamin use of 15 years or more was not associated with risk for advanced (1.10 [0.80–1.50], P trend =0.46), lethal (1.04 [0.83–1.31], P trend =0.13), or high-grade (0.98 [0.77–1.24], P trend = 0.37) prostate cancer compared to never-users ( Table 3 ).

disease_scope_review.endpoint_excerpt: Compared to never-users, men who used multivitamin 10 or more tablets per week had similar risk of advanced (HR: 1.14, 95% CI: 0.77-1.70, P<sub>trend</sub>=0.46) or lethal (HR: 1.07, 95% CI: 0.80-1.44, P<sub>trend</sub>=0.59) prostate cancer, and multivitamin use of 15 years or more was not associated with risk of advanced (HR: 1.10, 95% CI: 0.80-1.50, P<sub>trend</sub>=0.46) or lethal (HR: 1.04, 95% CI: 0.83-1.31, P<sub>trend</sub>=0.13) prostate cancer.
disease_scope_review.reason: The supplied HR of 1.14 compares at least 10 tablets per week with never use for incident advanced prostate cancer, an explicitly aggressive endpoint.

endpoint_case_count.excerpt: We documented 7,108 incident prostate cancer cases including 564 advanced and 1,065 lethal.
endpoint_case_count.reason: The HR of 1.14 is for advanced prostate cancer. The abstract explicitly reports 564 advanced cases in the relevant cohort; the separately reported 1,065 lethal cases correspond to a different endpoint.

summary_html:
No matching published aggressive prostate cancer baseline is available. These saved summaries use the HR ≈ RR ≈ OR identity approximation; provide incidence in Settings for baseline-dependent calculations.

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 2 studies yielded an overall effect size of 1.27 (95% CI: 1.04–1.56), suggesting that multivitamin is associated with a higher risk of aggressive prostate cancer. These findings were supported by low between-study heterogeneity (I² = 0.00%), indicating consistent findings across the included studies.

human_review_preserved_scope.reason: Separate aggressive-cancer endpoint evidence is unchanged by this general-incidence review
